Money is good, but you have to earn it and spend it. It's best to avoid money that's not easy to earn. Other companies might be fine, but the Shanxing Group isn't so easy to deal with. While it's a multinational corporation, that Korean company does have considerable capital.

Putting out her cigarette, Qian Yuling narrowed her eyes. She didn't want to rely on Zhao An; that would be the ultimate incompetence.

Since she couldn't find a replacement, she'd just leave this mess to Shanxing Group. She'd move everything out that wasn't covered in the contract. paragraphs: Jia Li's eyes lit up, then dimmed a little. "No, I need to help run the shop. Mom can't handle it all by herself."

Just then, a woman emerged from the kitchen. Despite her work, she'd taken good care of herself, her skin still fair. She wore red-rimmed glasses, looking serious yet with a hint of flirtation. "Meifeng, Xiaojun?"
"Hello, Auntie," the two women replied in unison.

My eldest cousin's eyes lit up. What a beautiful mature woman! I hadn't expected my aunt to be quite pretty, too. "Where's my uncle-in-law? Where's my cousin? I think he graduated from college, right?"

"Not yet. He's preparing for an internship this year." My aunt shook her head. She hadn't been in touch with her sister, Zhao Xinlei, much to her dismay. They'd all been struggling, and now that her sister was prosperous, she felt a little embarrassed to visit. They didn't contact each other regularly, and when they did, it was to ask for favors, which was truly embarrassing.
"Did you find a job?" My eldest cousin pressed, as if calculating something.
"I don't know. He said he's attending a training course, doing some kind of internship. Anyway, come, sit down. I'll make some tea," my aunt invited, a hint of sadness on her face.

"No, we're here to visit Xiaoli. You'll have a rest today. This thousand is for you. Don't be polite. Take it. I'm not short of money. Come on, Meifeng, take Xiaoli. Let's go out and have some fun." My eldest cousin generously offered money to pave the way, then pulled my cousin away.

My aunt had no time to stop her. She looked at the money on the table and the three people who had left, and shook her head bitterly. She really needed the money. She was about to turn and leave when her husband came in.
Jia Dafu's eyes welled up at the sight of the ten bills on the table. "That's just enough. Keep an eye on it. I'll be out for a bit." He took the money without even looking back.

My aunt sighed, knowing her husband had used the money to play mahjong. Business had been slow in recent years, and her husband had become increasingly decadent, gradually becoming addicted to gambling. No amount of persuasion could stop him, and for the sake of the family, the woman could only endure it again and again.

The eldest cousin and her husband took her cousin Jia Li to a high-end restaurant for dinner and then to the shopping street to buy clothes. They bought her designer clothes, each piece costing several thousand yuan.
Jia Li was stunned by this lavish spending, and felt a hint of envy.

We haven't spoken in ages. How's your family doing lately? If you need any help, just ask us. We're your sisters, and it's our duty to help you, your younger sister," the older cousin said generously. With Zhao An as her backer, she had no shortage of resources.

Actually, we filmed a scene last night, and today's livestream would have been very effective. Sharing some secrets and revealing some gossip would have been exciting and attracted a lot of traffic. The older cousin didn't do it. Her popularity has stabilized at around 500,000, and she doesn't have any big ambitions.
She used to want to make money from livestreaming, but now it's just a hobby, and she's mostly just enjoying life.

"It's okay, actually. It's just not been going well lately. My brother and his roommate took some training course that costs hundreds of yuan per class. They say they want to be celebrities. My dad's addicted to gambling, and the family business isn't doing well. Oh, oh, I don't know what to do." Jia Li began to cry as she spoke, as if she was speaking of something deeply saddening.
Ding Meifeng hugged her cousin and comforted her, "Okay, okay, it's okay. Everything will be fine. I'm here. You said you had a boyfriend at school. Is that true?"
Jia Li nodded shyly. "Yeah, yes, we just wrote love letters."

At least in terms of user experience, Android is very user-friendly. The sliding screen is also innovative. Almost all current phones have buttons, while newer phones have a single screen without buttons, significantly increasing the screen area. It's also very easy to use; you can figure it out after a few tries, no advanced education required.

"Let's start production now, starting with spare parts. We'll be self-sufficient and won't need to rely on anyone." Qian Yuling tested it herself and was very satisfied with the phone's performance. As a product, it's a very good one, offering excellent value for money.
"How much are you going to sell it for? What's the price?" Tang Yin narrowed her eyes, standing next to Qian Yuling, looking more like a pair of sisters than a mother and daughter.

"One thousand nine hundred and ninety-nine." Qian Yuling thought for a moment before naming the price. This wasn't something Zhao An had told her, but something she had determined based on various factors.
"What's the wholesale price?" Tang Yin pressed again. Her expression was now focused. She'd been fed yesterday, and not a single lustful thought crossed her mind.

"No wholesale price. This time, I'm going to build my own website. It's fine to use Zhao An's platform, but I'll earn the most profit by selling directly!" Qian Yuling was quite assertive. Considering how many distributors there are nationwide, these distributors control numerous offline store resources, a crucial factor for any brand in any industry.
Middlemen profit entirely from the price difference, which invisibly lowers manufacturers' profits. Trying to bypass them seems a bit unrealistic.
Mobile phones are nothing special; they still need physical storefronts to back them up. That's reassuring. Otherwise, who can they turn to if problems arise?

"That's not bad either. Not relying on anyone. Haha, you're truly a business silver fox. You've figured everything out. This road isn't going to be easy. Are you sure you can make it? The pressure will be immense," Tang Yin asked one last time. This wasn't a threat, but a fact. "Zhao An will handle this, daughter. You need to be smarter. Since you've already made an investment, you should at least get some interest back, rather than being treated as a plaything." Qian Yuling's eyes flickered. She was indeed smart, and there were things she could definitely handle, but there was no need.
Seeing Tang Yin's slightly thoughtful expression, Qian Yuling continued, "Women should act a little foolish. That way, men will think they can control us and be more willing to give."

"Can you control Zhao An?" Tang Yin suddenly asked a strange question.

"Control? I haven't thought of it that way. It's unrealistic. Striving for greater benefits within our own boundaries is what we should do. Men are lustful, so you get the point, don't you?" Qian Yuling's words were already quite clear. Some things can't be spoken out loud; only by understanding them can one truly grasp the true meaning.

Even then, Zhao An was entertaining other relevant personnel. The expansion of the food delivery platform would undoubtedly require support from all sides, and he had cunningly given away 30% of his shares—not to anyone else, but to the management.
This would directly reduce a significant portion of the resistance, allowing him to still make money without any other worries.
Whenever he wanted to withdraw, he could simply hand over power and wait for the monthly dividends. The whole process would be smooth and extremely safe.
